rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: England, Wales and Scotland: from 29 June 2026, section 44 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 makes it an offence to possess a sound moderator for a section 1 firearm unless the person holds a firearm certificate or a shotgun certificate. A certificate variation is no longer required for that accessory. The section does not extend to Northern Ireland. Shotgun and air-weapon moderators are a separate case.

rules.title: Night hunting
rules.notes: England and Wales: Deer Act 1991 section 3 makes it an offence to take or intentionally kill any deer between the end of the first hour after sunset and the start of the last hour before sunrise, subject to the exceptions in sections 6 and 8. This section does not state the law in Scotland or Northern Ireland. The GOV.UK class licence CL55 said it could be used until 31 July 2026, so it is not treated here as a current permission to shoot deer at night.

rules.title: Blaze orange / high-vis clothing
rules.notes: No statute requiring blaze-orange hats or vests for hunting was confirmed for this pack. The Deer Act 1991 does not mention high-visibility clothing. That is not proof that no other rule does.

rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: Firearms and Offensive Weapons Act 1990, section 7, as enacted: possession, sale or transfer of a silencer is an offence unless a superintendent of the Garda Síochána for the district where the person lives authorises it in writing. The superintendent must be satisfied that the person holds a firearm certificate for a firearm the silencer can fit, that the possession will not endanger public safety or the peace, and that the person has a special need sufficient to justify the authorisation. Conditions may be attached. The authorisation may last no longer than one year and may be revoked. This is the enacted section. Later amendments were not re-read for this pack.
rules.sourceTitle: Firearms and Offensive Weapons Act 1990, section 7

rules.title: Night hunting
rules.notes: Wildlife Act 1976, section 37, as enacted: subject to section 42, a person shall not hunt a woodcock between sunset and sunrise, or any other protected wild bird other than a wild duck or wild goose, or any protected wild animal, from one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise. Subsection (2) excepts hunting under stated ministerial licences. This is the enacted section. Later amendments were not re-read for this pack.

rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: Two official texts, both read on 9 November 2026, cover different parts of this. Classification: décret n° 2018-542 of 29 June 2018 rewrote article R. 311-1 of the Code de la sécurité intérieure. Section IV says a sound moderator is not a weapon when it is an add-on part that does not change how the firearm works. Acquisition: the same decree added article R. 312-45-2. Nobody may acquire a sound moderator without showing one of the titles in article R. 312-53 (a validated French or foreign hunting permit, a delegated shooting-federation licence, or a collector card) and the detention title for the matching firearm. Use while hunting: the consolidated arrêté of 1 August 1986, in force on 9 November 2026, article 2, no longer lists a ban on a device that quiets the shot. That line is in older copies of article 2, including the text shown as in force on 3 September 2008, and it is not in the current article 2. This is not a statement that every firearm authority or département allows a moderator. Check the current code article and the firearm's own papers before buying or fitting one.
rules.sourceTitle: Décret n° 2018-542 (Code de la sécurité intérieure R. 311-1 and R. 312-45-2); arrêté of 1 August 1986, article 2

rules.title: Night hunting
rules.notes: Arrêté of 1 August 1986, in force on 9 November 2026: article 2 bans lights and mirrors used to make capture or killing easier. Article 11 bis bans searching for or pursuing game with lights, except counts and captures authorised for science or restocking. The national hunters' federation, which is not the statute, describes daytime as from one hour before sunrise until one hour after sunset, with waterfowl flight times and registered night hides as exceptions. Those clock times are not copied here as a code article. Confirm the Code de l'environnement before relying on them.
rules.sourceTitle: Arrêté du 1er août 1986, articles 2 and 11 bis

rules.title: How named hoofed quarry may be shot
rules.notes: Arrêté of 1 August 1986, article 4, in force on 9 November 2026, names red deer, fallow deer, mouflon, chamois or isard, roe deer and wild boar. They may be shot only with a bullet, or with a hunting bow under the bow-hunting rules. A prefect may allow roe deer to be shot with shot on part of a department. Buckshot for wild boar in a driven hunt needs a ministerial order. This article does not set the open season. Département dates are not stored in this pack.

rules.title: Blaze orange / high-vis clothing
rules.notes: Arrêté of 5 October 2020, article 1: every participant in a collective driven big-game shoot, armed or not, must wear the fluorescent vest in article L. 424-15 so it stays visible the whole time. The vest may be part of a bright T-shirt, jacket or cape. The order does not say solitary stalking, or an orange hat on its own, is covered.

rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: Weapons Act (Waffengesetz) section 13(9), on gesetze-im-internet.de: the earlier paragraphs of that section apply to sound moderators as well. Sound moderators covered by that sentence may be used only with long guns that are permitted for hunting, with centre-fire ammunition, and only for hunting and hunting practice. The licensing paragraphs were not copied in full here.

rules.title: Night hunting
rules.notes: Federal Hunting Act (Bundesjagdgesetz) section 19(1) number 4: it is forbidden to kill cloven-hoofed game, except wild boar, and feathered game at night. Night runs from one and a half hours after sunset until one and a half hours before sunrise. The ban does not cover gulls, woodcock, capercaillie, black grouse or rackelhahn. The Länder can change hunting times under section 22. Species dates are not stored in this pack.

rules.title: Blaze orange / high-vis clothing
rules.notes: Sections 19 and 22 of the Federal Hunting Act, read on 9 November 2026, do not mention blaze-orange hats or vests. That is not proof that a Land has no clothing rule.

rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: Lei n.º 5/2006, consolidated text read on 9 November 2026. A silencer is defined as an accessory fitted to the muzzle to eliminate or reduce the noise of the shot. A sound moderator is a homologated accessory that removes up to 50 dB. Silencers, and sound moderators that are not homologated or that reduce the sound by more than 50 dB, are class A. Homologated sound moderators with a maximum reduction of 50 dB are class C. Class C weapons and accessories need prior authorisation from the national director of the PSP. Using a sound moderator on a firearm that is not class C is an offence (fine of €400 to €4,000).

rules.title: Sound moderator / silencer
rules.notes: Law 157/1992, article 21(1)(u), text in force on Normattiva read on 9 November 2026: it is forbidden for anyone to use firearms fitted with a silencer. The same letter also forbids shot on ungulates and several other means. Article 13(5) forbids every hunting weapon and means that article 13 does not explicitly allow. Silencers are not in that list.

rules.title: Night hunting
rules.notes: Articles 13 and 21, read on 9 November 2026, do not state a general night-hunting ban, so no yes or no is stored. Article 13(2-ter) does allow night-vision aiming devices, including digital ones, for selective wild-boar culling in the forms the law provides, except devices that are military materiel under Law 185/1990, article 2. That is an aiming-device rule, not a season.
